summary: IGNIS-PSI is an interactive spacecraft fire-safety and partial-gravity risk assessment platform powered by normalized microgravity ($0g$) combustion data from the NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository (psi.nasa.gov). Future Lunar ($1/6g$) and Martian ($3/8g$) habitats operate in hypobaric, oxygen-enriched atmospheres where standard $1g$ Earth flammability tests fail, while conventional AI dashboards suffer from retrieval opacity, hallucination, and single-variable bias. IGNIS-PSI solves this by unifying 55 unique planar combustion runs across six PSI investigations (SAFFIRE-I/II/III, BASS, BASS-II, ACME-BRE), ranking experimental analogs via a deterministic physics-informed Rational Quadratic proximity kernel, bracketing partial-gravity flame-spread rates between $0g$ and $1g$ bounds, and generating citation-audited engineering briefs. This transparent decision-support tool enables aerospace engineers to evaluate material ignition risks and export simulation-ready parameters without black-box guesswork.
details:
How It Works IGNIS-PSI operates across three integrated layers:

  • Normalized PSI Dataset: Consolidates 55 unique planar combustion records across six NASA PSI investigations (SAFFIRE-I/II/III, BASS, BASS-II, ACME-BRE), covering five material classes, 15%–40% $\text{O}_2$, 8.2–14.81 psi, and 2–30 cm/s airflow.
  • Physics-Informed Ranker: Couples $\text{O}_2\%$ and total pressure via oxygen partial pressure ($P_{\text{O}_2}$) and scores experimental proximity using a bounded Rational Quadratic similarity kernel. Stratified sorting prevents gaseous burner proxies (ACME-BRE) from crowding out exact solid-material matches (Nomex, Silicone), while interpolating $1/6g$ Lunar and $3/8g$ Mars flame-spread bounds between $0g$ PSI maxima and $1g$ Earth baselines.
  • Interactive Cockpit & Constrained SI Briefs: A Streamlit dashboard enables users to evaluate mission benchmarks (ISS, Lunar Habitat, Mars Transit, Apollo 1/Mir) or custom parameters, inspect a 2D empirical support heatmap, generate schema-enforced, citation-audited engineering briefs (gemini-3.8-flash with a deterministic offline fallback), and export dual-unit (NASA + SI) CSV matrices for simulation tools like MATLAB.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Auditable Decision-Making: Eliminates black-box AI hallucinations by tracing every risk score and engineering summary directly to verified NASA test_id records.
  • Space & Earth Dual-Use: Supports cabin material qualification and atmosphere design for Artemis Lunar habitats and Mars transit vehicles, while offering terrestrial value for high-oxygen enclosed environments such as hyperbaric oxygen chambers, submarines, and mine-rescue operations.

Tools & Tech Stack

  • Languages & Data: Python, JSON, CSV, NASA PSI (psi.nasa.gov) test matrices and metadata.
  • Backend & AI: FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic, Google GenAI SDK (gemini-3.8-flash), and a custom Leave-One-Out / Precision@3 evaluation suite.
  • Frontend: Streamlit and Plotly.

Creativity & Engineering Considerations

  • Transparent Extrapolation Mapping: Replacing opaque vector retrieval with a heavy-tailed Rational Quadratic physical kernel and a 2D empirical support manifold visually distinguishes tested flight regimes from extrapolation zones without score collapse under extreme stress conditions (50% O2).
  • Fidelity & Data Integrity: Weights vehicle-scale and solid-fuel experiments above gaseous proxies, preserves null spread rates where NASA archived only ignition/extinction outcomes, and validates retrieval accuracy offline (Precision@5 = 1.00, Sustained-Spread F1 = 0.827).
